items.title: No costing of trial-week follow-up that includes patient costs
items.whyItMatters: The review found no economic evaluation from the patient perspective (claim c5), and the manager's question is about where costs land.
items.opportunity: Cost the change from both perspectives and report them separately as well as combined.

items.title: Consequences can be hidden inside an average cost
items.whyItMatters: A saving per episode can coexist with more same-day reviews or emergency attendances for a few patients.
items.opportunity: Use a cost-consequence table that lists unplanned attendances, infections and on-time implant decisions next to costs.

items.title: Year-on-year comparison can absorb other changes
items.whyItMatters: Staffing, referral mix or lead technology may change between 2026 and 2027.
items.opportunity: Record co-interventions, compare case mix, and run a sensitivity analysis restricted to patients with a single trial lead type.

items.title: Patients who cannot use a telephone review
items.whyItMatters: The randomised comparison excluded people with hearing impairment or needing an interpreter; they may keep in-person visits and costs.
items.opportunity: Offer in-person day 3 on request, record who takes it, and report costs by this group.

items.title: Patient costs before the change were not recorded
items.whyItMatters: 2026 travel costs must be estimated from postcodes, while 2027 costs can be asked directly.
items.opportunity: Estimate both years from postcode distance with the same method, and use the 2027 questionnaire only to check the estimate.

errorsFound: The need frames the question as one number; a single net cost would hide the consequences the service manager also cares about.
reevaluation: The gaps favour a transparent cost-consequence analysis with separate perspectives and a consequences table, not a single incremental ratio.
summary: Five gaps: missing patient-perspective costing, hidden consequences, year-on-year confounding, equity of access to telephone review, and unrecorded patient costs before the change.
